review.headline: Dominant central control leads to a swift miniature

sections.text: You handled the Petrov's Defense cleanly from the start. After 5.Qe2 Qe7 6.d3 Nf6, queens were traded on e7, leaving you with an easy development path. White gave you the bishop pair with 9.Bxf6 Bxf6, and you immediately seized the open e-file with 10...Re8+.

You stepped up the pressure in the center with 11...d5, forcing White's knight away and picking up a pawn via 12...Bxb2. When White moved the rook with 13.Rb1, you went for a pin against the knight on d2 and the king on e1 using 13...Bc3, though simply dropping back to e5 was even cleaner.

White panicked under the central tension and blundered with 14.Rd1 instead of active options like 14.Nxd5. You developed smoothly with 14...Be6, and once White castled into safety with 15.O-O, your push 15...d4 locked down the position and forced White's resignation.

review.turning_point: White's blunder 14.Rd1 left their pieces completely tied down, allowing you to cement your spatial grip and seal the win.
review.focus: When retreating an active piece under attack, consider central squares like 13...Be5 rather than creating pins that can be unraveled.

review.headline: A wild tactical skirmish ends in a decisive material sweep

sections.text: Your opponent brought their queen out early against your Scandinavian Defense setup. Instead of punishing moves like 4...Qc5, you chose 7.b3, which slowed down your central development compared to pushing 7.d4. When Black jumped in with 8...Nd4, you simplified with 9.Nxd4 Qxd4 and then lashed out with 10.Nb5, unleashing a discovered attack from your bishop on b2 against the queen on d4, though it left your bishop undefended.

Black missed the chance to capture your bishop on b2 and played 10...Qe4+ instead. You answered with 11.Qe2, setting up a skewer along the e-file toward e6. Black then blundered with 11...Qc2, which allowed your knight to jump in with 12.Nxc7+, executing a fork against the king on e8 and the rook on a8.

You snatched the rook with 13.Nxa8, allowing 13...Qxb2 and creating chaos around your king after 14.Qd1. However, Black overextended with 14...Ne4 and 15...Nf2, giving up the knight to 16.Kxf2. When Black retreated with 17...Ke8, you found 18.Nc7+ Kd7 19.Nxe6, winning the bishop and trading into a totally winning endgame after 21.Qd3 Qxd3 22.Bxd3.

review.turning_point: Black's 11...Qc2 walked directly into 12.Nxc7+, a fork that netted you heavy material and broke open their position.
review.focus: Focus on keeping your king safe and developing pieces before hunting material, as seen when 13.Nxa8 let Black create counterplay against your uncastled king.
